prompt:
You are sitting in the cockpit looking out at the depths of space, with panels of electronics around you, whirring bleeps and lights, and the sleek, subtle glow of gently used screens. Combine the analog buzz and grit of Alien and Star Wars with sleek modern screen light and the digital-crush character of Asteroids.

Rebuild this whole hangar composition as exciting ink-drawn sci-fi fantasy equipment. This is a new composition using the references below, not a trace of either example menu. Output a full 16:9 game menu concept.

Image 1 is the chosen ink-and-shade FINISH only: weighted black contours, graphic shadow planes, tactile wear. Image 2 supplies the real nebula and recognizable Vanguard ship and livery. Images 3 and 4, the beige consoles, supply recessed screen housings, secondary mechanisms and function-key-style tabs. Image 5, the dark cockpit, supplies purposeful electronics, grouped amber/green lights and layered dark equipment. Images 6, 7 and 8 supply the SCREEN language: Nostromo's strong inverse title strips, MU/TH/UR's raster mono lettering, and the thick rules/hatching in the oxygen display. These are mood images, not their labels, characters or rooms.

The only menu is on the actual console screen. Use a single terminal ledger with an inverse off-white HANGAR title strip, a narrow category/tab column and a wider monospaced value column. Place these exact five lines once:
SHIP            Vanguard
ENGINE          Default_Engine
SHIELD          Default_Shield
PRIMARY         Lasers
SECONDARY       Missiles
Small selection chevrons belong beside the values. Integrate LAUNCH into the same equipment assembly. Use warm off-white on a dark phosphor screen, terminal raster type, tick rules and hatched separator strips. Every line must be present. Screen language should be recognizable as the supplied terminals, with decisive graphic contrast.

The ship is the large hero of the open scene, fully visible with generous breathing room near the upper center/right. Equipment is a grounded assembly in the LOWER foreground with a readable, nearly front-facing screen. Rich dark graphite chassis, warm-grey highlights, useful vents, service connectors, cable guards and layered housing shapes, all drawn with the selected bold ink/shadow finish. Concentrate amber/dim green lamps in a few purposeful groups. Hardware details and the screen should be exciting and clearly visible.

Correct the three failures from the earlier attempt: show the loadout ONLY inside the physical screen; remove the source screenshot's old menu; leave the upper view open without a full canopy/window arch or full-height side walls. Use hatched dividers, not invented progress bars or numerical telemetry. The console remains attached to visible dark supports descending out of the bottom edge. Reusable corners and straight edges use roughly 40-degree chamfers. Keep all five actual values readable. No presentation captions.

COMPOSITION A: low navigation station. One wide, low console slopes toward the viewer from the LOWER LEFT, supported below. The screen is a broad terminal ledger. Two dark shoulders around it carry compact electronics and lights. LAUNCH lives at the right end of this localized assembly. The console occupies the lower foreground, leaving a broad unbroken nebula view around the hero ship and open space to the right of the equipment. Do not span the entire lower edge with a bright slab. Keep the detail strong.
